abstract: Overflow metabolism describes the excretion of partially oxidized metabolites into the extracellular environment during rapid sugar utilization. Although these metabolites can later be reused, it remains unclear whether reassimilation also occurs during ongoing sugar consumption, and if so, how. Here, 13C-isotope tracing and metabolic flux analysis of acetate exchange in Saccharomyces cerevisiae during hexose utilization reveal that net acetate overflow is only the small difference between order-of-magnitude larger simultaneous excretion and assimilation fluxes. Unlike ethanol production, acetate exchange is not determined by hexose uptake but depends on metabolic processes downstream of glycolysis. Ethanol oxidation contributes to acetate excretion even during net ethanol production, directly linking the two main overflow pathways. We exploited this understanding to redirect extracellular acetate into the acetyl-CoA-derived product mevalonate. These results establish acetate overflow as a dynamic exchange linking ethanol turnover to acetyl-CoA metabolism, in which acetate is simultaneously an overflow product and a carbon source that can be redirected toward bioproduction.
